name: Freedom Holding Corp.
moat_justification: Kazakhstan's #3 financial group and a real digital ecosystem (SuperApp bundling brokerage, banking, insurance, payments and lifestyle; 858,000 brokerage accounts; Freedom Life #3-tier insurance shares) — but it trails Kaspi.kz and Halyk Bank in its home market, digital brokerage/banking switching costs are low, it competes for deposits on price, and returns have not proven the franchise: ROE fell to 6.2% in FY2025 and 10.3% in FY2026 (fundamentals.json) from 26.4-32.6% in FY2023-24, i.e. at or below the cost of equity in the two most recent years, with net income swinging $76M-$379M across the last three fiscal years. Regulatory dependence is a structural erosion force: a Kazakhstan insurance-law change cut net insurance revenue 29% in FY2026, and the group carries an SEC Wells Notice (March 2026), the 2023 Hindenburg allegations overhang, and founder (Timur Turlov) concentration.
fragility_flags: BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2017 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.4% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Kazakhstan's #3 financial ecosystem (brokerage/banking/insurance SuperApp), moat 4/10 — GAAP-profitable every year since FY2018, but at $181.57 the base OE yield is 1.4% on the NI-based base of $2.51/share: weighted IRR 5.2%, IV@15% $34.56, even the super-bull case only 8.2%; clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$35.
moat_for: Integrated SuperApp ecosystem bundling brokerage, banking, insurance, payments and lifestyle — ~2.6M monthly active users in March 2026 (S&P), cross-sell across 8.7M ecosystem customers at Q1 FY2027
Leading Kazakhstan brokerage: ~858,000 customer accounts at FY2026 (+26% YoY), >56% funded
Real insurance niches per National Bank of Kazakhstan data in the FY2026 10-K reporting: Freedom Life ~19.3% of pension annuity premiums, Freedom Insurance ~14.53% of car-owner liability premiums
Top-3 Kazakhstan financial group by market capitalization, behind only Kaspi.kz and Halyk Bank; S&P upgraded core subsidiaries to BB- with positive outlook in 2026
Loyalty program converts cashback into fractional FRHC shares — customers are literally invested in the platform
moat_against: Only #3 in its home market: Kaspi.kz and Halyk Bank run larger ecosystems with bigger MAU and lending volumes; Freedom is the challenger, not the incumbent standard
Returns do not prove a moat: ROE 6.2% (FY2025) and 10.3% (FY2026) per fundamentals.json — at/below cost of equity — after 26.4%/32.6% in FY2023/24; net income ranged $76M-$379M over FY2024-26
Regulatory hostage in its core market: Kazakhstan legislation change cut net insurance revenue 29% in FY2026; banking/brokerage/insurance are all licensed, policy-sensitive businesses

Governance/regulatory overhang: SEC Wells Notice to the company and CEO (March 2026), 2023 Hindenburg allegations (sanctions evasion, related-party FST Belize), CFO resignation June 2026, Russian prosecutor lawsuit filed October 2026

Low switching costs and price competition: digital brokerage and deposits are rate-shopped (Freedom Bank's top tenge deposit pays 19.5% AER); founder control by Timur Turlov concentrates key-man and related-party risk
